summary: Clarify burst/quota interaction for high-frequency webhook callbacks counted against interactive route
description:
Issue summary: ParcelFlow reports a sudden increase in 429 throttles during their high-frequency webhook callback pipeline. The callbacks are delivered to an application route used for interactive reranking; callbacks arrive in bursts when upstream S3 presigned-url notifications replay.

Impact: Approximately 30% of webhook callbacks receive 429s during hourly replay windows. This causes delayed processing of delivery confirmations and downstream duplicate retries, increasing end-to-end latency and customer-visible SLA breaches.

Environment: Dedicated customer pool (dedicated-us-east-1) serving both interactive rerank and background webhook callbacks under a single API key. Traffic pattern: dozens of short lived signed-url callback connections per second for 10-20 minute replay windows; outside replay windows traffic is steady and low.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer enables S3 batch replay for 20k events over 15 minutes pointing at their rerank route.
2) SDKs create ephemeral signed URLs that fan out callbacks concurrently.
3) Callbacks hit the interactive /v1/rerank endpoint using the same API key as interactive UI traffic.
4) Observe 429s in callback logs and increased retry loops on customer side.

Observed behavior: 429s are reported with throttle headers indicating 'route' quota exhaustion rather than a background/bulk pool. Console shows the per-route token bucket depleting rapidly during replays; dedicated pool overall tokens are not fully exhausted. No obvious errors on serving-runtime.

Expected behavior: Background or bulk webhook callbacks should not deplete an interactive route's burst window in a dedicated pool when customer config has a separate burst pool for bulk workloads. Alternatively, callbacks should be routed to a separate route or API key so they draw from a different burst bucket.

Customer request: Clarify how burst/bucket accounting works for signed-url callbacks and recommend configuration changes or quick workarounds to prevent future replays from causing interactive 429s.

Asked customer for permission to apply a temporary policy change in their staging mirror to validate.

investigation_notes: Checked console metrics for tenant 'parcelflow-prod' between 2026-03-10 01:00 and 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC: per-route token window dropped to zero twice within a 15-minute window while tenant pool consumed ~40% capacity.

Examined rate-limiter service logs (rl-03) for correlated 'token_taken' events showing high frequency 1-2 token consumption per callback request; requests use HTTP/2 multiplexing which didn't change accounting but increased concurrency per connection.

Confirmed that route affinity config for the dedicated pool was set to 'route-priority' which assigns refill credits to route buckets first; this explains route bucket depletion even when tenant pool had spare credit.
Verified no recent deploys to rate-limiter or api-gateway between 2026-03-09 and 2026-03-10 that would affect accounting logic (checked related PRs in linked_github_prs).

Replayed 1k synthetic callbacks in staging with single API key: reproduced rapid route window depletion. Replayed with separate API key bound to background route: route window preserved for interactive traffic.
resolution_notes:
Temporary resolution: Advised ParcelFlow to create a dedicated API key for background webhook callbacks and bind it to a background-only route; they implemented this and confirmed elimination of interactive-route 429s during replays.

Recommended permanent actions: (1) Update dedicated-pool configuration docs to call out route-affinity behaviors and default 'route-priority' implications. (2) Expose route-vs-key quota mapping in Console (UX ticket created). (3) Offer a one-click policy in Console to allocate 'separate_burst_pool' for background routes.

Follow-ups: Engineering to add a safeguard that flags high-frequency callback patterns using UI/Console alerts; Product to review whether new accounts should default to 'tenant-priority' for mixed-traffic dedicated pools.

Related changes: We will open a small ops PR to add a console alert and a docs blurb; assigned to Priya for docs + Luca for verification.
